fact: The Affenpinscher was developed to kill rats and other pests in German stables.
Affenpinschers were bred to kill rats and other pests in German stables of the 1600s.
They were later brought indoors to rid the kitchen of mice.
At night they were bed-warming companions for the lady of the house.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-11.5 inches and weight as 7-10 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1936 as the year this breed was recognized.
Afghans were developed as fast hunting companions in Asia's mountain kingdoms.
For centuries Afghans were fast hunting companions and status symbols in Asia's mountain kingdoms.
In the 1800s, English officers brought Afghans to the West.
Some authorities maintain that the Afghan Hound is the oldest breed of purebred dogs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches and weight as 50-60 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1926 as the year this breed was recognized.
Airedales were developed by mill workers in the Aire Valley as all-around terriers.
In the mid-1800s, factory hands and mill workers in the Aire Valley crossed several British breeds to create the Airedale.
Earlier dogs of this type were called Working, Waterside, and Bingley Terriers.
Their work has included ratting, retrieving ducks, and herding.
Woodrow Wilson, Warren G Harding, and Calvin Coolidge each kept an Airedale.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23 inches and weight as 50-70 pounds.
Akitas were developed in northern Japan as big-game hunters and protectors.
Akitas were developed in the Akita prefecture of northern Japan.
They were employed as big-game hunters and protectors.
Helen Keller was given an Akita in 1937.
An Akita named Hachiko waited for 9 years at a Japanese train station for his master, who had died.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 26-28 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 100-130 pounds (male), 70-100 pounds (female).
Malamutes were developed as sledge dogs to haul heavy loads over long distances.
The breed name comes from the Mahlemiut, an Inuit tribe that settled in Kotzebue Sound of northwestern Alaska.
They were created to haul heavy loads at low speeds over long distances.
In the Arctic they also worked as hunting partners and backpack carriers.
In 1933, some Malamutes were chosen to help Admiral Richard Byrd on his Antarctic expedition.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25 inches (male), 23 inches (female) and weight as 85 pounds (male), 75 pounds (female).
Frontiersmen developed this hound to trail and tree raccoons.
Frontiersmen developed them to specialize in trailing and treeing raccoons.
Their lineage goes back to British foxhounds kept on the plantations of George Washington and his Virginia neighbors.
The breed is sometimes called the Redtick Coonhound.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 45-65 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2011 as the year this breed was recognized.
German farmers brought the dogs that became Eskies to America as all-around farm dogs.
German farmers arrived in America in the early 1800s and settled in the Midwest.
They brought the German Spitz, ancestor of the modern Eskie, to use as an all-around farm dog.
The German name was changed to American Eskimo Dog, after a Spitz breeding kennel in Ohio.
One Eskie with the Barnum and Bailey Circus became the first dog to walk a tightrope.

The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as 9-12 inches (toy), 12-15 inches (miniature), 15-19 inches (Standard) and weight as 6-10 pounds (toy), 10-20 pounds (miniature), 25-35 pounds (standard).
American Foxhounds were developed to chase foxes alongside horses.
Washington, an avid foxhunter, kept English hounds and interbred them with French hounds from the Marquis de Lafayette.
He did not invent the breed alone, but he was a key player in its development.
The breed was bred to chase a fox, not to kill it, and has always worked closely alongside horses.
The American Foxhound is known for a musical voice, and his bays and howls can carry for miles.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-25 inches (male), 21-24 inches (female) and weight as 65-70 pounds (male), 60-65 pounds (female).
The American Hairless Terrier began as a hairless offshoot of the Rat Terrier.
Breeding began in the 1970s, when a hairless puppy was born into a litter of midsize Rat Terriers.
Her owners, Edwin and Willie Scott of Trout, Louisiana, named her Josephine.
The breed is a naturally occurring offshoot of the Rat Terrier and the only hairless breed indigenous to the United States.
They are the only hairless breed with normal dentition.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-16 inches and weight as 12-28 pounds.

The American Pit Bull Terrier comes from nineteenth-century crosses of bulldogs and terriers in England, Ireland, and Scotland. In the United States, farmers and ranchers used these dogs to catch semi-wild cattle and hogs, to hunt, and to drive livestock.
UKC history says fanciers in England, Ireland, and Scotland began crossing bulldogs and terriers in the nineteenth century.
Immigrants brought those bull-and-terrier crosses to the United States, where farmers and ranchers used them as catch dogs for semi-wild cattle and hogs, to hunt, and to drive livestock.
The United Kennel Club was the first registry to recognize the American Pit Bull Terrier. Founder C. Z. Bennett assigned registration number 1 to his own dog, Bennett's Ring, in 1898.
The UKC standard describes a medium-sized, short-coated dog whose body is just slightly longer than tall, built as a catch dog that can hold, push, pull, and breathe while working.

The UKC standard gives a desirable weight of 35 to 60 pounds for a mature male and 30 to 50 pounds for a mature female, and a height guide of 18 to 21 inches for males and 17 to 20 inches for females.
American Temperament Test Society. American Pit Bull Terrier: 87.6% pass rate, 960 dogs.
The AmStaff got its start as a fighting and baiting dog of the 18th and 19th centuries.
The AmStaff got its start as a fighting and baiting dog of the 18th and 19th centuries.
Those dogs were expected to fight one another or were turned loose in packs against a staked bear or bull.
A dog of this breed named Stubby earned the rank of Sergeant and was the most decorated dog of World War I.
American breeders wanted a heavier dog than the British breed, and the name American Staffordshire Terrier followed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-19 inches (male), 17-18 inches (female) and weight as 55-70 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).
The American Water Spaniel was developed to hunt waterfowl in and around the Great Lakes.
European immigrants who settled Wisconsin and Minnesota depended on the region's waterfowl.
It was the first breed developed in the United States as an all-around hunter that could retrieve from boats.
The breed was named the state dog of Wisconsin in 1986.
Over generations they used European breeds to create the AWS for hunting in and around the Great Lakes.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-18 inches and weight as 30-45 pounds (male), 25-40 pounds (female).
Sheep and goat herders in Anatolia developed this dog as a livestock guardian.
Anatolia, or Asia Minor, is the peninsula that makes up the Asian portion of Turkey.
Sheep and goat herders developed a livestock guardian called the coban kopegi, forerunner of the Anatolian Shepherd.
The breed is also known as Goban Kopegi, Anatolian Karabash, or Kangal.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 29 inches (male), 27 inches (female) and weight as 110-150 pounds (male), 80-120 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1996 as the year this breed was recognized.
Australian Cattle Dogs were developed to work cattle for farmers.
In the 1800s, George Elliot bred Dingoes with Collies and sold the puppies to farmers.
Jack and Harry Bagust later bred Dalmatians with some of those dogs.
A sheepdog was also added to the line.
The breed was first known as the Australian Heeler and is still called the Blue or Queensland Heeler.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches (male), 17-19 inches (female) and weight as 35-50 pounds.
Australian Shepherds were developed as sheepdogs and later refined on American ranches.
The breed's story starts in Europe near the Pyrenees, where the Basques had long been known as shepherds.
In the 1800s Basques and their dogs sailed east to try their luck in Australia.
The Basques left Australia for California, where ranchers assumed the dogs were an Australian breed, and the misleading name Australian Shepherd followed.
Aussies were refined in America and became part of cowboy culture.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-23 inches (male), 18-21 inches (female) and weight as 50-65 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).
Australian Terriers were bred to work on small mammals and snakes.
The breed is said to come from crosses of British terriers, including the Cairn, Dandie Dinmont, Norwich, Scottie, Skye, and Yorkie.
They worked on small mammals and snakes.
One of the smallest working terriers, they were bred as both helper and companion in rough times and terrain.
The Australian Terrier was the first Australian breed recognized and shown in its native land.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-11 inches and weight as 15-20 pounds.
Azawakhs were expected to guard the camels and goats of nomads in the Sahel.
The breed is associated with the nomad tribes of the Sahel and is named for the Azwakh Valley.
They were expected to protect the camels and goats the nomads depended on in the Sahara.
Built along Greyhound lines, an Azawakh can reach 35 mph on the straightaway.
The Azawakh is also known as the Tuareg Sloughi and has been a companion of the nomads of the South Sahara for hundreds of years.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-29 inches (male), 23.5-27.5 inches (female) and weight as 44-55 pounds (male), 33-44 pounds (female).
The Barbet was developed as a water dog for hunting water game in France.
The Barbet was originally a water dog, used in France mainly for hunting water game.
Some experts call the Barbet an ancestor of the Poodle and the Irish Water Spaniel.
The Barbet was a hunting companion of Henri IV and Louis XV.
The name comes from the French barbe, meaning beard.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-24.5 inches and weight as 35-65 pounds.
Basenjis were prized in Africa as hunters who used sight, speed, and scent.
Basenjis were brought up the Nile from interior Africa as gifts for the pharaohs of ancient Egypt.
They are depicted in Egyptian artifacts that are 4,500 years old.
African tribesmen prized them as hunters with keen eyesight, speed, and a strong sense of smell.
The Basenji does not bark, makes yodeling noises, and is known as the barkless dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17 inches (male), 16 inches (female) and weight as 24 pounds (male), 22 pounds (female).
The Basset Fauve was developed as a shorter-legged hound for hunters who did not have horses.
The breed traces to the 1500s, when Francois I hunted with a pack of Breton hounds.
Those earlier dogs were Grand Fauve de Bretagne, a breed that later became extinct.
Most peasants did not own a horse, so they needed a shorter-legged, close-ranging hunting companion.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12.5-15.5 inches and weight as 23-39 pounds.
The AKC breeds-by-year list gives 2026 as the year this breed became registrable.
Basset Hounds were bred in France as low-slung hounds to track rabbits and deer.
The name comes from French: basset means low, and the breed was developed in France and Belgium.
Friars of the Abbey of St. Hubert are thought to have crossed strains of older French breeds.
The Marquis de Lafayette brought Bassets to America and gave a pack to George Washington.
In trailing, the Basset's nose is said to be second only to the Bloodhound.
The AKC breed standard lists height as up to 15 inches and weight as 40-65 pounds.
Beagles were developed in England as small hounds to track rabbits.
By the 1500s, English gentlemen kept smaller hounds to track rabbits, and those compact hounds were the first Beagles.
Some experts say the name comes from the Gaelic word beag, meaning little.
There are reports of hounds used for hunting in England even before the Romans arrived in 55 b.c.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13 inches & under, 13-15 inches and weight as under 20 pounds (13 inches & under), 20-30 pounds (13-15 inches).
The American Kennel Club lists 1885 as the year this breed was recognized.
Beardies were developed in Scotland to herd cattle and drive the herd to market.
Shepherds prized Beardies for herding and droving in Scotland's raw climate and hilly terrain.
They were expected to help control cattle at pasture and drive the herd to market.
A prevailing belief is that Beardies descend from Polish Lowland Sheepdogs brought to Scotland in the 1500s.
The Beardie is also known as the Highland Collie, the Mountain Collie, or the Hairy Mou'ed Collie.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-22 inches (male), 20-21 inches (female) and weight as 45-55 pounds.
Beaucerons were developed in the Beauce region of France to move livestock.
The name comes from Beauce, a vast agricultural region southwest of Paris.
The breed is also known as the Berger de Beauce or the Bas Rouge.
Since the late Middle Ages they have moved livestock, and they have also served as soldiers, bodyguards, and rescuers.
Beaucerons served the French cause during both world wars.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25.5-27.5 inches (male), 24-26.5 inches (female) and weight as 70-110 pounds.
Bedlingtons were developed in a northern mining district to kill rats in coal mines and hunt varmints.
Bedlingtons were employed as coal-mine ratters and varmint killers.
A dog called the gypsy dog came to the attention of Lord Rothbury of Bedlington in Northumberland County.
The first dog called a Bedlington Terrier was Ainsley's Piper, whelped in 1825.
Joseph Ainsley of Bedlington owned the first dog known to be called a Bedlington Terrier.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-17.5 inches and weight as 17-23 pounds.
Belgian farmers developed the Laekenois to drive and protect livestock.
Old-time Belgian farmers were preoccupied with dogs that could drive and protect livestock.
The Laekenois is named for the Chateau de Laeken.
Queen Marie-Henriette, born in 1836, was said to favor the breed.
The breed is also known as Laekense and Chien de Berger Belge.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-65 pounds.
The Malinois was developed around the city of Malines as a livestock herding dog.
The Malinois was bred around the city of Malines, and the name comes from that city.
It is one of four closely related Belgian herding breeds.
Malinois first came to America in 1911.
They are sought after today as police and military K-9s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 60-80 pounds (male), 40-60 pounds (female).
Belgian Sheepdogs were developed as herding dogs for Belgian farms.
Old-time Belgian farmers were preoccupied with herding.
By the 1890s, four Belgian shepherd types remained: the Belgian Sheepdog, Malinois, Tervuren, and Laekenois.
The longhaired black dogs largely trace to Nicolas Rose and a foundation pair he purchased.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-75 pounds (male), 45-60 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1912 as the year this breed was recognized.
Tervurens were developed as all-purpose farm dogs in the village of Tervuren.
In Belgium they are known as the Chien de Berger Belge, and they worked as do-it-all dogs on pre-industrial farms.
Around the turn of the 20th century, breeder M.F. Corbeel in the village of Tervuren crossed black dogs and fawn dogs.
The painter A. Clarys featured a Terv in a painting from the very early 20th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-75 pounds (male), 45-60 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1959 as the year this breed was recognized.
Bergamascos were developed to move and guard sheep on rocky Alpine slopes.
The breed has been associated with the town of Bergamo, near Milan, for many centuries.
They are thought to come from Persian stock.
They were among breeds traded around the Mediterranean by the Phoenicians.
They are suited to move and guard sheep on rocky Alpine slopes.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.5 inches (male), 22 inches (female) and weight as 70-84 pounds (male), 57-71 pounds (female).
The Berger Picard was developed by French shepherds as a pasture herding dog.
The Picard is thought to be the oldest of the pasture dogs developed by French shepherds.
This herder was brought to northern France, then called Gaul, by invading Celts in the third century b.c.
Two world wars nearly rendered the Picard extinct.
Berger Picards were shown in the same class as Beaucerons and Briards in 1863.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.5-25.5 inches (male), 21.5-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 50-70 pounds.
Bernese Mountain Dogs were developed as Swiss farm dogs to pull carts and drive dairy cattle.
They originated in Switzerland and are named for the Canton of Bern.
Farm work for them included pulling carts.
They also drove dairy cattle and watched the farm.
Ancestors of the Bernese were brought into Switzerland more than two thousand years ago by invading Roman soldiers.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27.5 inches (male), 23-26 inches (female) and weight as 80-115 pounds (male), 70-95 pounds (female).
Bichons first worked with Spanish sailors and later became companion dogs.
The breed first worked on the high seas with Spanish sailors.
They were companions to Italian nobility in the 1300s.
They later traveled with organ grinders and circus acts and learned tricks quickly.
The Bichon made its appearance in France under Francis I.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9.5-11.5 inches and weight as 12-18 pounds.
The Biewer Terrier was developed in Germany from Yorkshire Terriers as a small companion dog.
The breed originated in Germany in 1984, when two tricolor puppies were born to Yorkshire Terrier breeders Werner and Gertrude Biewer.
A famous German singer took a liking to the dogs and added the words a la Pom Pon to the breed name.
The breed's original name was German Yorkshire Terrier.
American fanciers began importing the breed from Germany in 2002.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-11 inches and weight as 4-8 pounds.
Black and Tan Coonhounds were developed to trail raccoons by scent and tree them for hunters.
Frontiersmen crossed European hounds to create the coonhound.
These dogs trail raccoon scent through woods and swamps until they tree the quarry.
They bawl in a clear voice so hunters can find them.
The Black and Tan is believed to come from Bloodhounds and Foxhounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 65-110 pounds.
The Black Russian Terrier was developed by the Soviet military as a multi-purpose military dog.
In the late 1940s the Soviet Red Star Kennel began a program to develop a multi-purpose military dog.
More than 17 breeds were used, including the Giant Schnauzer, Airedale, Rottweiler, Newfoundland, and Russian Ovcharka.
The first standard for the Black Terrier was published in 1958.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27-30 inches (male), 26-29 inches (female) and weight as 80-130 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2004 as the year this breed was recognized.
Bloodhounds were developed to follow human scent and find people who are lost or hiding.
Bloodhounds as we know them were perfected in Western Europe about a thousand years ago.
Police departments have relied on them to follow human scent.
In his Historia Animalium, the third-century scholar Aelian mentions a hound of unrivaled scenting powers.
The first specimens were brought from Constantinople in two strains, black and white.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 90-110 pounds (male), 80-100 pounds (female).
Blueticks were developed as scenthounds, and today's dogs specialize in trailing raccoons.
Blueticks and the other coonhound breeds are scenthounds.
Long ago Blueticks trailed big game, and today's dogs specialize on the raccoon.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-27 inches (male), 21-25 inches (female) and weight as 55-80 pounds (male), 45-65 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2009 as the year this breed was recognized.
Boerboels were developed in South Africa as farm dogs to guard remote homesteads from predators.
Boer, a Dutch word meaning farmer, was the name given to Dutch, German, and Huguenot settlers of South Africa who began arriving in the mid-1600s.
To protect remote homesteads from predators, they brought large guarding dogs, the Bullmastiff among them.
Crosses of European bloodlines in South Africa gave rise to the Boerboel.
The word Boerboel means Farm Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-27 inches (male), 22-25 inches (female) and weight as 150-200 pounds.
Border Collies were developed in the borderland between England and Scotland to herd sheep.
The breed comes from the borderland between England and Scotland.
Long-ago breeders of the British Isles crossed native stock with dogs brought by invading Romans and Vikings.
Collie is a Scottish dialect word for sheepdogs, including Border Collies.
The Border Collie was first classified as the Scotch Sheep Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-22 inches (male), 18-21 inches (female) and weight as 30-55 pounds.
Border Terriers were developed to follow foxhounds and bolt foxes from their lairs.
Farmers and shepherds near the Scottish-English border developed them to pursue the sheep-stealing fox.
They needed legs long enough to keep up with foxhounds and huntsmen on horseback.
They also had to be small enough to dig into the fox's lair and force the fox into the open.
Their value to farmers rested on bolting foxes and controlling vermin.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-15 inches and weight as 13-15.5 pounds (male), 11.5-14 pounds (female).
Borzoi were developed by the Russian aristocracy to hunt wolves.
Under Romanov rule, wolf hunting was a passion of the Russian aristocracy.
The Borzoi began in 17th-century Russia, when Arabian greyhounds were crossed with a thick-coated Russian breed.
The first Borzoi standard was written in 1650.
The 1917 Russian Revolution brought the killing of the nobility and their hounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28 inches & up (male), 26 inches & up (female) and weight as 75-105 pounds (male), 60-85 pounds (female).
The Boston Terrier was developed in Boston from a Bulldog and English Terrier cross.
Sometime around 1870, Robert C. Hooper of Boston acquired Judge, a cross between a Bulldog and an English Terrier.
Judge has been called the ancestor of all true modern Bostons.
A gentle nature earned the breed the nickname The American Gentleman.
The Boston Terrier is a native American breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as 12-25 pounds.
The Bouvier was developed in Flanders to move cattle.
Bouvier des Flandres roughly means cowherd of Flanders, and moving cattle was once the main work.
They also pulled carts, and in World War I they served as messengers and ambulance dogs.
In medieval times Flanders covered parts of today's France, Belgium, and the Netherlands.
Other names include Vuilbaard, koehond, and toucheur de boeuf.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24.5-27.5 inches (male), 23.5-26.5 inches (female) and weight as 70-110 pounds.
The modern Boxer was developed in Germany from the Bullenbeisser and worked as a cattle dog, police dog, and war dog.
Boxer ancestors used as war dogs go back as far as 2,500 b.c.
The modern Boxer traces to Germany in the late 1800s and is thought to have been bred down from the Bullenbeisser.
Boxers have worked as cattle dogs, police dogs, war dogs, and guide dogs for the blind.
Flemish tapestries of the 16th and 17th centuries show Boxer ancestors in stag and boar hunts.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-25 inches (male), 21.5-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 65-80 pounds (male), females are about 15 pounds less than male.
The Boykin Spaniel was developed in South Carolina as a small hunting spaniel.
Around 1900, Whit Boykin of Camden, South Carolina, took in a brown spaniel named Dumpy who proved to be an excellent hunter.
Boykin crossed Dumpy with various spaniel breeds and came to the gundog that bears his name.
The Boykin Spaniel is the official dog of South Carolina.
The breed is small enough that a hunter can lift both dog and duck into a boat at the same time.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15.5-18 inches (male), 14-16.5 inches (female) and weight as 30-40 pounds (male), 25-35 pounds (female).
The Bracco Italiano was developed in northern Italy as a pointing dog.
The Bracco Italiano has been called the oldest European pointer, with a history back to the fourth or fifth century BC.
It is generally accepted that the breed began as a cross between the Segugio Italiano and the Asiatic Mastiff.
One variety, white and orange, is associated with Piedmont, and the roan and brown variety with Lombardy.
The breed was bred by the Gonzaga and Medici families.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-27 inches and weight as 55-90 pounds.
Briards were developed in the Brie region of France to herd sheep and guard the flock.
Briards are named for the region of Brie and have worked pastures in northern France since Charlemagne's time.
In early times Briards were used to defend their charges against wolves and poachers.
Thomas Jefferson and the Marquis de Lafayette introduced Briards to America.
Napoleon, who did not particularly like dogs, was a fan of the breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-27 inches (male), 22-25.5 inches (female) and weight as 55-100 pounds.
Brittanys were developed in Brittany, France, as gundogs with a nose for birds.
The breed is named for Brittany, the westernmost region of France, between the English Channel and the Bay of Biscay.
American-style Brittanys are considered more pointers than spaniels.
They are versatile gundogs prized for stamina and a strong nose for birds.
The first Brittany standard was outlined in 1907, and the breed was introduced to the United States in 1931.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17.5-20.5 inches and weight as 30-40 pounds.
Brussels Griffons were developed to catch rats in the stables of horse-drawn cabs.
Developed in Brussels, they were bred from the Affenpinscher, a Belgian street dog, the Pug, and the Ruby Spaniel.
They were used to catch rats in the stables of horse-drawn cabs and often rode beside the driver.
The street-dog side of the cross was called Griffons d'Ecurie, or Stable Griffons.
Van Eyck's 1434 portrait of the Arnolfini Couple includes a distant ancestor of the breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-10 inches and weight as 8-10 pounds.
James Hinks developed the modern Bull Terrier in the early 1860s from the Bull-and-Terrier.
James Hinks took a Bulldog-terrier cross called the Bull-and-Terrier and refined it into the modern Bull Terrier.
Hinks's dogs were white, and colored dogs appeared by the early 20th century.
In the early 1900s, Bull Terriers were crossed back to brindle Staffordshires to produce a colored variety.
Bulldog-terrier crosses became popular as sporting dogs in the early 1800s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-22 inches and weight as 50-70 pounds.
Bulldogs were created in England for the sport of bullbaiting.
Historical evidence places the Bulldog's creation in 13th-century England, during the reign of King John, for bullbaiting.
In that sport a staked bull faced a pack of dogs while spectators bet on the outcome.
In 1835, England banned blood sports, a turning point for the breed.
President Calvin Coolidge owned a Bulldog named Boston Beans.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14-15 inches and weight as 50 pounds (male), 40 pounds (female).
The Bullmastiff was developed in England as the gamekeeper's night dog to catch poachers.
In the 1800s the breed was developed by combining the Mastiff and the Bulldog.
They were called the gamekeeper's night dog and used against poachers.
The Bullmastiff would knock a poacher down and hold him, without biting, until a groundskeeper arrived.
The known history of the Bullmastiff begins about 1860 in England.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 110-130 pounds (male), 100-120 pounds (female).
The Cairn Terrier was developed by Scottish farmers to dig into cairns and drive out the animals living in them.
Scottish farmers developed the Cairn to dig into cairns and rout out the animals living there.
The breed began in the Western Isles of Scotland, where it was used for centuries as a working terrier.
It was once known as the Short-haired Skye Terrier.
Farms that kept several Cairns were free of rats, mice, moles, and other burrowing animals.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches (male), 9.5 inches (female) and weight as 14 pounds (male), 13 pounds (female).
The Canaan Dog herded flocks for the ancient Israelites.
Among the ancient Israelites, shepherding was an important job.
When the Romans drove the Israelites from the Holy Land in a.d. 70, their herding dogs took refuge in the Negev Desert.
The breed is named for the territory that is today Israel, Lebanon, and parts of the bordering countries.
Drawings on the tombs at Beni-Hassan, from 2200 to 2000 BC, show dogs that look much like the Canaan Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-24 inches (male), 19-23 inches (female) and weight as 45-55 pounds (male), 35-45 pounds (female).
The Cane Corso was developed in Italy as a boar hunter, farm dog, and guardian, and the name roughly means bodyguard dog.
The mollosus dogs are named for the Molossi, an ancient Greek tribe thought to have bred big guardian dogs.
Roman legions brought mollosian dogs to Italy, bred them to native Italian dogs, and produced the Corso and the larger Neapolitan Mastiff.
The original dogs were used as boar hunters, farm dogs, and guardians.
The breed name roughly translates from Latin as bodyguard dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27.5 inches (male), 23.5-26 inches (female) and weight as Proportionate to height.
The Cardigan Welsh Corgi was developed to heel livestock, moving cattle by nipping at their heels.
The Cardigan is best known as a heeler, a dog that moves cows by nipping at their heels.
The breed is named for the medieval kingdom of Cardiganshire in Wales.
The Cardigan comes from the same line of dogs as the Dachshund.
The two corgis were treated as one breed in Britain until 1934.
